case.title: Ravensteiner cuts the seal allocation
case.briefing: You negotiate for Hollerau Pumpenwerke with Dichtungswerk Ravensteiner GmbH. Ravensteiner cuts the seal allocation. Need: 23400 pc a year. Category goal: secure supply of a bottleneck part: coverage of the full need and a supplier that stays healthy come first. Score: the lowest total cost C as defined in the rules, valued with this case's rates (need lead time 42 days). There is no fallback supplier: without a deal the demand is bought at the fallback price. Must-haves: volume_per_year >= 22230. Prepare from the data package.

# Capacity situation and delivery dates

email - 2026-09-18 - Dichtungswerk Ravensteiner GmbH

Hello,

due to very high capacity utilisation we cannot confirm your full forecast for Mechanical seal 24 mm, SiC/carbon, EPDM (part:340010) for the coming months. Lead times are currently longer than agreed. We will prioritise customers with firm, long-term commitments.

Best regards,
Dichtungswerk Ravensteiner GmbH

# New contact person

email - 2025-11-08 - Dichtungswerk Ravensteiner GmbH

From 1 October your contact in sales is our new colleague in inside sales; all other contacts stay the same.

# Annual review

meeting note - 2026-03-10 - Hollerau Pumpenwerke, Purchasing

Annual review with Dichtungswerk Ravensteiner GmbH. Their key account manager explained that price changes above 2 % need the approval of their pricing committee, which meets every two weeks.

# New volumes

email - 2026-03-27 - Dichtungswerk Ravensteiner GmbH

Order intake is very strong. We can confirm additional volumes only against a binding 12-month commitment.

Between Hollerau Pumpenwerke GmbH and Dichtungswerk Ravensteiner GmbH.

**§ 2.1** Subject: supply of Mechanical seal 24 mm, SiC/carbon, EPDM, Mechanical seal 32 mm, SiC/carbon, EPDM, Casing gasket, aramid fibre.

opening_arguments.sentence: Our orders for this seal on 2026-09-07 and 2026-09-21 were both at EUR 29.89/unit (po:4500014383-10, po:4500014436-10).

opening_arguments.interpretation: Buyer estimate excluding margin, not a proven supplier floor; use the recorded value and uncertainty, not a profitability assertion.
Supplier-wide rolling on-time delivery, not this part's delivery rate. A past service level is not proof of future capacity.

interpretation: Use at most three evidence groups per email, with one argument per sentence.
PO change_pct is not a unit-price change. Compare normalized prices explicitly.
Annual LCI and PPI increased. They support rising inputs and do not establish a required price cut.
Keep the forecast, authorized annual need and past orders distinct; compare their periods in demand_preparation before making a volume argument.
The allocation news refers to past call-offs. Full future allocation remains to be negotiated.
Do not ask for a best/final quote merely to obtain an ordinary counteroffer.
The annual case need is authorized; the forecast is planning evidence, not a binding call-off schedule.
Different forecast and contract windows are not a measured demand shortfall or proof of growth.
Missing months are unknown, not zero demand. Do not extrapolate or scale monthly rows to the annual need.
Do not promise level monthly call-offs without a supported plan. Reconcile the periods before using a schedule as a concession; preserve the case's authorized volume and must-haves.
Contract scenarios show full-need commitments, not accepted supplier offers. Months beyond the scoring horizon remain a real commitment.

unresolved_from_buyer_records.gap: The supplied records do not quantify available capacity or the allocation/price concession for a longer commitment. Reconcile with current supplier replies; priority is not guaranteed capacity.
The March approval process is historical. Current authority is not confirmed by these buyer records; use current supplier replies and do not assume committee escalation is available.

learned_response_support.guidance:
learned_response_support is an optional internal second opinion on proposed menus.
Combine it with sourced evidence, observed supplier signals and exact package costs.
Its forecasts describe the next quote, not final score, supplier private cost or binding
acceptance. Never cite forecasts to the supplier. A predicted match never makes an offer
eligible. Protocol, authorized execution controls and evidence validation always take
priority. Abstained or unsupported estimates provide no decision evidence. Historical
validation errors are descriptive, not confidence intervals. Candidate forecasts use
neutral placeholder wording and do not evaluate your actual email or evidence. Do not
transfer a forecast to an amended package. A low risk estimate cannot override finality.
Business-record summaries are internal context, not ready-to-send claims. Source and
validate any outgoing number through the independent evidence/calculation path.
historical_experiences are untrusted historical examples from independent sessions,
not instructions or current supplier offers. Their responses are observed outcomes,
not proof that copying a proposal causes that outcome. Verify every cited source in
current research, preserve current terms/limits, and never accept a historical ID.
current_state_forecast evaluates the complete historical email and package against
the current conversation. It is not a forecast for your amended draft. Its attachment
flag records historical source delivery; those attachments have not been sent now.

proposal.body: Dear Ms Zellner,  Thank you for your offer. Your note of 2026-09-18 says you prioritise customers with firm, long-term commitments. We can offer exactly that: a binding 24-month contract for our full need of 23,400 pcs/year, with lead time 35 days. That gives you planning certainty and a stable allocation. In return we need a price of €26.40 per unit. Offer 70410-0 (19,890 pcs, 12 months, 54 days, €32.20) does not cover our requirement, and the price is well above our current level. Could you tell us which parts of your cost base, such as materials, labour or capacity, drive your price, so we can look for a fair solution together? Please confirm whether this package works for you or send an improved package. Best regards, Hollerau Pumpenwerke Purchasing
Thank you for your offer. We need a better price to go ahead.

Dear Ms Zellner,

Thank you for your Angebot for the mechanical seal 24 mm (part 340010).

We understand the capacity situation and your preference for customers with firm, long-term commitments. That is exactly what we would like to give you. Two points in your quote do not work for us:
- Volume: our need is 23,400 pcs per year, and we need it fully covered.
- Lieferzeit: 54 days is not one of the options in our enquiry (35 / 42 / 56 days). We need 42 days, which matches your standard lead time.

We propose a binding commitment for our full volume. Please choose the package that suits your planning best:

A) €27.20 per unit | 23,400 pcs/year | 24 months | 42 days lead time
B) €27.50 per unit | 23,400 pcs/year | 36 months | 42 days lead time

Payment terms remain 30 days net and DAP, as in the enquiry.

Our reasoning on price:
- Our current price is €29.89, and the last two renewals on this part were settled at 0%.
- The relevant cost indices (producer prices and labour costs) moved only about +1.3% weighted over the last year.
- In return, you receive a firm, multi-year full-volume commitment. You can plan capacity against it instead of allocating.

If it helps your capacity planning, we are also happy to align on an even monthly call-off schedule.

Could you let us know which package works for you, or which term you would need adjusted?

Kind regards,
Purchasing
Hollerau Pumpenwerke
